title: Strip dangerous caps from gsr-kms-server and btop
head: 8a07b82e265f
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Stable omarchy PKGBUILD does not ship either new libalpm hook
leads.consequence: The recipe explicitly installs just the three old hooks, though it ships both helper binaries (lines 111-125) and stamps both new migration markers for freshly created users (lines 148-157). A new stable install never installs either capability-strip hook and never runs either migration for its fresh user. The Arch btop package includes cap_perfmon/cap_dac_read_search, and gpu-screen-recorder post_install/upgrade applies cap_sys_admin; later upgrades retain/reapply those capabilities. Add both 90-omarchy-strip-btop-caps.hook and 90-omarchy-strip-gsr-kms-caps.hook to this explicit install list.

leads.summary: omarchy-dev's separate hook install list omits both capability-strip hooks
leads.consequence: Developer-package installations also ship the two new helper scripts and seed migration markers (lines 111-125,148-157), but no package-owned cap-stripping hooks, so fresh users of omarchy-dev do not strip btop or gsr capabilities on upgrades. Add both hook names to this recipe as well. Note omarchy-dev provides omarchy (line 14), so Depends = omarchy in the in-tree hook is satisfiable here; the missing recipe entries are the problem.

leads.summary: KMS helper check accepts inheritable-only CAP_SYS_ADMIN although recorder will use pkexec
leads.consequence: getcap can report cap_sys_admin in the inheritable set only, for example 'cap_sys_admin=i' or a combined list without p. The new substring test treats this as permission and chooses the KMS branch at lines 187-211. At 6.1.3, GSR checks CAP_SYS_ADMIN specifically in CAP_PERMITTED (kms_client.c:279-285); if absent, it launches pkexec at :340-342. Thus a non-default but valid file-capability configuration defeats the promise that KMS does not escalate unless explicitly requested. Parse the permitted bit, or use the same libcap predicate as the recorder; include a regression case for inheritable-only caps.
leads.triage: behavioural_sent_to_opus; opus followup-1 Q1: only non-standard cap sets; not realistic on Omarchy

leads.summary: Both new helpers and the modified recorder fail the repository-wide bin style test
leads.consequence: This test rejects raw 'command -v' outside designated omarchy-cmd/pkg scripts. The PR adds one invocation each in bin/omarchy-strip-btop-caps:8, bin/omarchy-strip-gsr-kms-caps:13, and bin/omarchy-capture-screenrecording:166. The sandboxed test exits 1 listing those three exact paths, so test/shell and CI fail until changed to approved helper calls or the rule is updated deliberately.

leads.summary: Post-transaction helpers silently claim success even when the capability removal fails
leads.consequence: Both execute setcap -r ... || true, and also return success when setcap cannot be found or the binary is not executable. With a real setcap error (for example permission/unsupported xattr) the post-transaction hook reports success and the existing cap remains; on the next upgrade the package reinstalls the cap and the same helper silently fails again. setcap itself can print an error on stderr, but no failed hook status/retry or user-facing diagnostic is provided. Check getcap/verify the cleared xattr and propagate a real failure; treat an already-absent cap separately.
leads.triage: behavioural_sent_to_opus; opus followup-1 Q2: same xattr outcome either design; not materially worse

leads.summary: A getcap failure is treated as no capability, and the migration is stamped as complete
leads.consequence: The checks gate on command -v setcap but not getcap, then use getcap | grep -q . inside if under bash -euo pipefail. Missing getcap or a read error takes the false branch, no capability is removed, the migration installs its hook and exits 0, and omarchy-migrate touches the marker at :91-96. Thus a subsequent run will not retry the original strip, even if the executable still carries its cap (unless another qualifying package upgrade triggers the hook). libcap getcap itself logs several errors but returns zero rather than distinguishing them, so check for tool availability and verify the resulting xattr before stamping.
leads.triage: behavioural_sent_to_opus; opus followup-1 Q3: getcap/setcap ship together in libcap; not realistic

leads.summary: Default recording no longer supports the documented drag-to-select region flow
leads.consequence: With the capability stripped, default recording, including the menu/hotkey no-audio and webcam actions, goes directly to -w portal without calling select_capture_target (the freeform slurp picker). GPU Screen Recorder's portal implementation offers MONITOR, WINDOW and VIRTUAL source types, not a freeform region. Users who previously dragged a sub-monitor rectangle can no longer do so by default, and the manual and agent capture skill still promise a region picker. Either restore a safe region path (without pkexec) or update docs and explain how users may regain region capture with an explicit KMS override after restoring the cap.

leads.summary: Migration-created /etc hooks are never removed with Omarchy and have no Depends guard
leads.consequence: The migrations install unowned /etc/pacman.d/hooks files referencing /usr/bin/omarchy-strip-* with no Depends. When omarchy/omarchy-dev is removed, these files survive and override any same-name packaged hooks. A later btop or gpu-screen-recorder install/upgrade triggers an action for a missing executable, producing a failed post-transaction hook after the package was changed. The in-tree hooks include Depends = omarchy, but cannot supersede these higher-priority /etc copies. Add Depends to migration-installed copies and define a cleanup path for already installed hook copies.

leads.summary: The package hook fixture list omits both newly added hook entries
leads.consequence: The existing alpm_hooks loop is the project's cross-repository check that each package-owned hook is explicitly installed to /usr/share/libalpm/hooks. It only enumerates the three old hooks; the PR appends presence checks at lines 432-444 that pass even though both recipes do not install the new hooks. Add 90-omarchy-strip-btop-caps.hook and 90-omarchy-strip-gsr-kms-caps.hook to alpm_hooks (lines 177-181) and check both stable and dev recipe lists if both are supported.

leads.summary: Changed portal-backend comment repeats an HDR capability the shipped recorder explicitly denies
leads.consequence: The edited comment says the portal covers HDR, but gpu-screen-recorder 6.1.3 warns that portal capture does not support HDR, and tonemaps HDR codecs to SDR instead. This does not establish a new HDR regression (the old comment also claimed HDR); it makes the advertised reason to prefer portal misleading. Qualify this comment and any user guidance rather than promising HDR preservation.
leads.triage: factual_verified_not_published; gsr 6.1.3 main.c:596-599 confirms portal tonemaps HDR, but the HDR claim pre-exists in the base comment; nitpick

leads.summary: The new GSR regression test passes when all three behavior changes are disabled
leads.consequence: It only checks that source files contain particular strings, not whether stripping occurs, whether absent CAP_SYS_ADMIN chooses the portal, or whether migration strips a capability. A sandboxed mutant made the helper a no-op, made the migration conditional always false and set use_portal=false on the absent-cap path; with the expected strings retained in comments or the separate override branch all three test assertions still passed under LC_ALL=C. Add sandboxed behavior cases for setcap, migration and actual -w backend selections (plus the inheritable-only case).

limits: The current-base merged recorder and config-test have no conflict markers (merged/result/), but running the entire current-base test suite against combined code was not established.
Open PR statuses and diffs are saved in open-prs/; comparisons show 17 inspected heads diverged. Cross-PR combined fixtures were not run, so no cross-PR conflict is claimed.

flags.claim: Keep a non-interactive route for agents, for example by leaving `--fullscreen` on KMS or documenting the prompt.
flags.why: Once the capability is stripped, KMS capture is not non-interactive: gsr runs `pkexec gsr-kms-server` and shows an admin authentication prompt, running the helper as root, which is what the PR removes. 'Documenting the prompt' is not a non-interactive route either.

flags.claim: This PR reverses that for every migrated install without mentioning it.
flags.why: The PR does mention preferring portal: the script comment (head bin/omarchy-capture-screenrecording:17-19, 181-184) and the folded PR #11716 description ('When the capability is absent, prefer portal capture...'). What it does not acknowledge is that this makes portal the default on every migrated install, reversing the earlier opt-in decision and its known portal failure. My own final-report F2 ('the PR does not surface it') has the same overstatement.

omarchy-settings also installs named files from default/ elsewhere, including one libalpm hook: `00-omarchy-platform-guard.hook` into /usr/share/libalpm/hooks, guarded by `if [[ -f ... ]]`. What is true is that the two new hook files reach only /usr/share/omarchy/default/libalpm/hooks/.

flags.claim: In a sandbox case with a symlink to a non-regular target, the migration replaced the symlink and stripped the capability.
flags.why: The wrong setup is described. The sandbox case used a dangling symlink (its target did not exist) inside the private root, not a symlink to a non-regular file. The results are right: the path became a regular file, the target was not created and the capability was stripped.

flags.claim: A mutant that inverts the portal fallback, ... still passes (exit 0).
flags.why: The previous sentence names both gsr-kms-caps-test.sh and the config-test.sh additions, but only gsr-kms-caps-test.sh was run on the mutant. config-test.sh was not run.

flags.claim: Stubbing `getcap` on `PATH` and asserting the recorder's `-w` argument ... would cover the behavior.
flags.why: Part of the suggestion is missing. The script first checks `[[ -x /usr/bin/gsr-kms-server ]]` with a hard-coded path, so stubbing getcap alone cannot drive the capability-present branch on a test host without that file. The test needs an overridable helper path (or `command -v gsr-kms-server`). My harness had to substitute the path for this reason.

flags.claim: keep `cap_perfmon` (for example `setcap cap_perfmon=ep /usr/bin/btop`) and drop only the DAC bypass
flags.why: A qualifier is lost. Keeping cap_perfmon brings back only the Intel GPU stats. CPU package power still needs the DAC bypass, because RAPL energy_uj is 0400. Read in context ('loses CPU package power and Intel GPU'), the option looks as if it restores both.

flags.claim: Once the migration strips the capability, `gsr_kms_has_sys_admin` is false and every mode takes the portal path.
flags.why: The 'by default' qualifier is missing: with OMARCHY_SCREENRECORD_USE_KMS=true (and USE_PORTAL unset), head takes KMS even when the capability is stripped.

flags.claim: The repository test rejects raw `command -v` in `bin/` outside `omarchy-cmd-*`/`omarchy-pkg-*`.
flags.why: Nitpick: the rule also exempts `omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro`. The rest of the finding checks out (see the checked list).

flags.claim: ... point `Exec` at a missing binary on each btop or gpu-screen-recorder transaction
flags.why: Nitpick: the hooks trigger only on Install and Upgrade, not on removal or other transactions.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** on an existing install that runs the new migrations, both capabilities are stripped and stay stripped across later package upgrades. The `PostTransaction` hooks run after the Arch `gpu-screen-recorder` scriptlet that re-applies `cap_sys_admin=ep`, the migrations are idempotent, and the new `getcap` check agrees with gpu-screen-recorder's own direct-helper-or-`pkexec` decision for the capability sets Arch and upstream apply. Five issues remain: fresh installs are not covered, the repository's style test fails, the default recording flow changes, the migration leaves unowned hook copies, and btop loses two monitoring features.

### The new hooks are not installed as pacman hooks, so fresh installs keep both capabilities

`default/libalpm/hooks/` is not read by pacman directly. In omarchy-pkgs, the `omarchy` and `omarchy-dev` PKGBUILDs install three named hooks into `/usr/share/libalpm/hooks/` (no glob), and `omarchy-settings` copies `default/` to `/usr/share/omarchy/default/`, so the two new hook files land only there. No companion omarchy-pkgs change was found; the closed #11512 noted that "omarchy-pkgs still needs the one-line hook install", and this PR's description does not carry that forward.

Fresh installs also never run the migrations: `omarchy-provision-user --first-install` marks every shipped migration as done.

```text
existing install:  migration strips caps + writes /etc/pacman.d/hooks copy  -> stripped, portal
fresh install:     migrations pre-marked, hooks not packaged                -> caps kept, KMS (as on base)
```

**Impact:** based on source reading, fresh installs keep `cap_sys_admin=ep` on `gsr-kms-server` and `cap_dac_read_search,cap_perfmon=ep` on btop, so the two install populations end up with different security state and different recording behavior. The `alpm_hooks` packaging check in `test/shell.d/config-test.sh` was not extended, so the suite does not catch this.

**Suggested change:** add install lines for both hooks to the `omarchy` and `omarchy-dev` PKGBUILDs in omarchy-pkgs, and add both names to `alpm_hooks` in `config-test.sh`.

### `test/shell.d/bin-style-test.sh` fails on the new `command -v` calls

The repository test rejects raw `command -v` in `bin/` outside `omarchy-cmd-*`, `omarchy-pkg-*` and `omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro`. At the PR head it fails (exit 1, `not ok - bin commands use command helpers`) listing exactly `bin/omarchy-capture-screenrecording`, `bin/omarchy-strip-gsr-kms-caps` and `bin/omarchy-strip-btop-caps`. The base has no violations, and the test is unchanged on the current `quattro` tip.

**Suggested change:** use `omarchy-cmd-present getcap` / `omarchy-cmd-present setcap` in place of `command -v`.

### Portal becomes the default recording backend, and `--fullscreen` becomes interactive

Once the migration strips the capability, `gsr_kms_has_sys_admin` is false and every mode takes the portal path unless `OMARCHY_SCREENRECORD_USE_KMS=true` is set. Recorder arguments from a stubbed backend matrix (60 cases per variant):

| Input | Base | Head, capability present | Head, capability stripped |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--fullscreen` | `-w <focused monitor>` (KMS) | same as base | `-w portal` |
| default, region picked | Omarchy picker, then `-w WxH+X+Y` | same as base | `-w portal`, Omarchy picker not shown |
| `USE_PORTAL=true` + `--fullscreen` | `-w <focused monitor>` | `-w portal` | `-w portal` |

**Impact:**
- `--fullscreen` was added for agents (commit `83e7f413`), and Omarchy's agent skills tell agents to use it. The script does not pass `-restore-portal-session`, so the portal share picker opens (per gsr 6.1.3 and xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland source) and the script waits until a person picks or cancels.
- Base keeps portal opt-in on purpose: the unchanged header comment says "Off by default because the portal path can fail EGL DMA-BUF modifier import on some configurations", and commit `6a5e5378` is "Bypass portal by default for screenrecording due to portal bug". The PR's script comment says it prefers portal, but neither the PR nor the comment addresses that earlier decision or the portal failure behind it, and the change applies to every migrated install. How often that portal failure occurs was not established.
- The region-picker flow in `manual/12-screenshots-recording.md` and the webcam overlay's region anchoring no longer describe the default.

The trade-off itself is defensible: without the capability, KMS capture makes gsr run `gsr-kms-server` through `pkexec` as full root, with an authentication prompt.

**Suggested change:** state the default change in the PR description so maintainers can decide on it, update the "Off by default" header comment and the manual, and document `OMARCHY_SCREENRECORD_USE_KMS`. Note that after the strip, agents have no non-interactive route: KMS needs a `pkexec` prompt and portal needs a pick, so the agent docs for `--fullscreen` need updating too. Passing `-restore-portal-session yes` could let later recordings reuse the previous selection (untested; the first recording would still need a pick, and the restored source is the last one picked, not the focused monitor).

### The migration's `/etc/pacman.d/hooks` copies become a second, unowned source of truth

Both migrations write hooks into `/etc/pacman.d/hooks/` using the same file names as the in-tree hooks, but without `Depends = omarchy`.

**Impact** (per pacman 7.1.0 source and `alpm-hooks(5)`):
- A same-named hook in `/etc/pacman.d/hooks` overrides a packaged one, so once the hooks are packaged, migrated systems keep running the `/etc` copy. The `[[ ! -f $hook ]]` guard means later hook changes never reach them.
- No package owns the copies, so they survive removal of `omarchy` and then point `Exec` at a missing binary whenever btop or gpu-screen-recorder is installed or upgraded (a non-fatal pacman error).
- A `/dev/null` mask symlink fails `-f`, so the migration replaces an administrator's mask. In a sandbox case with a dangling symlink in place of the hook, the migration replaced the symlink and stripped the capability.
- Because the hook re-strips on every gpu-screen-recorder upgrade, the documented `OMARCHY_SCREENRECORD_USE_KMS=true` "after restoring the capability" lasts only until the next upgrade, after which each recording goes through `pkexec`.

**Suggested change:** once the hooks are packaged, reduce each migration to stripping the current capability. If the `/etc` copies are kept, add `Depends = omarchy` and plan how they are removed.

### btop loses CPU package power and Intel GPU monitoring

`setcap -r` removes all of btop's file capabilities, including `cap_perfmon`, not only `CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH` as the commit title says. btop's README describes these capabilities as needed for Intel GPU and CPU wattage (btop 1.4.7 source):
- CPU package power reads `intel-rapl` `energy_uj`, which the kernel exposes as mode 0400.
- Intel GPU stats open CPU-wide perf events, which need `CAP_PERFMON` at the default `perf_event_paranoid` of 2.

**Impact:** Omarchy's shipped `config/btop/btop.conf` enables `show_cpu_watts` and Intel GPU display. After this change, btop run as a normal user no longer shows either (source reading, not run on hardware).

**Suggested change:** state this trade-off in the PR, or keep `cap_perfmon` (for example `setcap cap_perfmon=ep /usr/bin/btop`) and drop only the DAC bypass. That keeps Intel GPU stats; CPU package power would still need the DAC bypass. Either is a maintainer judgement call.

**Optional test improvement:** `test/shell.d/gsr-kms-caps-test.sh` and the `config-test.sh` additions only check file presence and grep for strings. A mutant that inverts the portal fallback, turns the strip helper into a no-op, moves the hook to `PreTransaction` and reduces the migration to its `echo` line still passes `gsr-kms-caps-test.sh` (exit 0). Making the hard-coded `/usr/bin/gsr-kms-server` path overridable, stubbing `getcap` on `PATH` and asserting the recorder's `-w` argument (as `screenrecording-test.sh` already runs the script with a stub recorder), plus a migration test with recorded `sudo`/`setcap` stubs, would cover the behavior.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Pinned head `8a07b82e`. Source review of the PR, omarchy-pkgs packaging, omarchy-iso, gpu-screen-recorder 6.1.3 with its Arch packaging, btop 1.4.7 with its Arch packaging, pacman 7.1.0, libcap and xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland. Sandboxed runs with stubbed `sudo`, `setcap`, `getcap` and recorder: a backend-selection matrix for base, head and a mutant, a migration harness, a test-mutation run and the repository's `bin-style-test.sh`. No real `pacman` transaction, capability change, `pkexec` prompt, portal session or btop hardware reading was exercised.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
